comparison.objective: Recover a spacer by pushing it through a covered channel, then place it in a nest; candidate depins one electrical terminal from a reusable connector housing.
comparison.physical_skill: PR uses aligned axial pushing and later pick/place. Candidate requires dual-blade insertion around a recessed contact, simultaneous tang depression, and coordinated opposite-side wire push/pull.
comparison.success_condition: PR requires a measured pusher-driven exit, nesting, tool return, release, and 1 s stability. Candidate requires only the selected terminal to exit rearward, neighbors retained, housing/crimp undamaged, and 3 s released stability.
comparison.reason: Both involve tool-assisted extraction, but the tested release mechanism and coordination are materially different: indirect channel pushing versus maintaining two-tang disengagement during a bimanual wire withdrawal.
